note: The major scale's steps (scales:3): the W and H steps of C major on the scale panel and the white keys of the piano, the same steps from G with the one black key that keeps them in place, then made-up tunes tapped on the staff that end on Do. C is the lesson (its half steps are the white keys with no black key between), so there are no moves; G is the second key, with a line on what stays the same.

exercise.title: C major: whole steps and half steps
exercise.why: A major scale is the same row of whole steps and half steps from any note, so once you know where its two half steps fall, you can build the scale in any key.

cells.text:
The panel below spells C major, and under each note it shows the step to the next one: W for a whole step, H for a half step. Press Play on the panel to hear the scale.
Then tap up the piano under it, from {{1}} to the next {{1}}. Between {{3}} and {{4}}, and between {{7}} and {{1}}, there is no black key: those are the two half steps.

The piano below shows G major. Tap from {{1}} up to the next {{1}}: the two half steps fall between {{3}} and {{4}} and between {{7}} and {{1}}, as in C.
To keep them there, one white key gives way to a black one, {{f-sharp}}, the 7th note. Tap {{7}}, then {{1}}.
Practice until you hear the half step from {{7}} to {{1}} before you tap it.

The staff below shows C major: tap a note to hear it. Make up short tunes by tapping, moving mostly by step, and end each one on a ringed {{1}}.
Then end a tune on {{7}} and wait, before you tap {{1}} to finish it.
Practice until you can hear where a tune wants to end before you tap the last note.
